58963.question_text: An electron of mass 9.1 x 10\(^{-31}\) kg moves with a speed of 2.0 x 10\(^6\) ms\(^{-1}\) round the nucleus of an atom in a Circular path of radius 6.1 x 10(^{11}\) m. Determine the angular speed of the electron.
58963.explanation:
Angular speed of the electron (W) 

w = \(\frac{Velocity}{Radius} = \frac{V}{R}\)

= \(\frac{2.0 \times 10^6}{6.1 \times 10^{11}}\) 

= 3.28 x 10\(^{16}\) rads\(^{-1}\)

58977.subject: Physics
58977.question_text:
An electron of mass 9.1 x 10\(^{-31}\) kg moves with a speed of 2.0 x 10\(^6\) ms\(^{-1}\) round the nucleus of an atom in a Circular path of radius

6.1 x 10\(^{11}\) m. Calculate the centripetal force acting on the electron.
58977.explanation:
Centripetal force (Fr) = \(\frac{MV^2}{r}\) 

i.e. Fr = \(\frac{Mv^2}{r}\) 

= \(\frac{9.1 \times 10^{-31} \times 2.0 \times 10^6 \times 2.0 \times 10^6}{6.1 \times 10^{-11}}\) N 

= (\(\frac{36.4 \times 10^{-19}}{6.1 \times 10^{-11}}\)) N

= 5.967 x 10\(^{-8}\) N 

~ 6.0 x 10\(^{-8}\) N
